**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 11:24
- [USER] User inquired about the cost of attendance for international students at Stanford University.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The breakdown of the cost of attendance for international students at Stanford University includes:
  - Tuition and fees: $54,015
  - Room and board: $17,287
  - Books and supplies: $1,245
  - Personal expenses: $3,015
  - Health insurance: $5,346
  - Total cost of attendance: $80,908
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Costs are estimates and may vary depending on the specific program and needs of the individual student; some graduate programs may have higher costs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended that international students consult with the Stanford University Office of International Affairs for the most up-to-date and accurate cost information.
- [USER] User expressed concern about the high cost of attendance for international students compared to domestic students and asked about support or assistance provided to them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Reasons for higher costs for international students include:
  - Non-resident tuition rates.
  - Additional fees for visa processing, travel, and insurance.
  - Higher living expenses without access to in-state or family support.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Stanford University provides support through the Office of International Affairs, which offers immigration advising, cultural adjustment, and academic support, along with programs and resources for international students.
- [USER] User asked if international students can apply for financial aid or scholarships to help offset costs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] International students can apply for financial aid and scholarships, but availability is limited:
  - Need-based financial aid is available for undergraduate international students.
  - No merit scholarships or need-based aid for international graduate students.
  - Required forms include the CSS/Financial Aid PROFILE and the Stanford Financial Aid Application.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Graduate students may find financial assistance through fellowships, grants, or scholarships from their respective departments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested that international students look for external scholarships or grants from private organizations or their home countries.
- [USER] User expressed disappointment about limited financial aid options for international graduate students and asked about other options to offset costs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional options for international graduate students include:
  - Research and teaching assistantships that provide stipends, tuition waivers, and health insurance.
  - External fellowships and grants from private organizations or home countries.
  - Part-time employment on-campus for up to 20 hours per week during the academic year.
  - Private student loans from banks in the U.S. or their home countries.
- [USER] User expressed frustration about the burden of higher costs
